title: Why did 1,000 world citizens bury their underpants?
gist: A citizen-science study buried cotton underpants at 1,000 sites in 25 countries to create a simple, visual 'underpants index' of soil health, finding land use (private gardens vs. lawns vs. farmland) is the dominant driver of soil biological activity.

insights.claim: Researchers led by Marcel van der Heijden (University of Zurich) recruited 1,000 volunteers across 25 countries to bury cotton underpants for 30 and 60 days as a low-cost, easy-to-interpret proxy for soil decomposition activity, validating it against the existing 'teabag index' (TBI) standard.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A cheap, scalable citizen-science methodology for soil biological health could be adopted by agritech, precision-agriculture, or soil-carbon-credit monitoring programs looking for low-cost proxies for soil biological activity.
insights.quote: Our results show that how soil is managed can significantly affect both soil life and soil quality.

insights.claim: Land use was found to be the most important factor in soil decomposition rates: private gardens showed the fastest decomposition and highest organic matter, while lawns showed the least biological activity, with farmland and meadows in between.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Reinforces that intensive lawn management (a common suburban/commercial landscaping practice) is worse for soil biology than gardens or even farmland, relevant to any ESG or land-management framework assessing soil carbon/biodiversity outcomes.
insights.quote: Underpants decomposed the fastest in private gardens, where soil analysis also revealed the highest levels of organic matter.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'The results: Land use was the most important factor'

insights.claim: The underpants method proved as informative as the more technically demanding teabag index while being more accessible for non-scientist volunteers, since it gives a direct visual and tactile decomposition read rather than requiring precise mass measurements.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A validated simplified soil-health assay lowers the barrier for large-scale citizen monitoring networks, which could feed into agricultural or environmental data collection at low marginal cost.
insights.quote: The underpants 'provide a direct visual and haptic measure of decomposition that is easier to interpret.'
